chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The lending of wealth is a barrier to the payment of Zakat.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying Zakat on money that has been lent out as a loan?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys that Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) established lending as a 'hima' (protected zone) from Zakat, a principle reflecting the juristic view that wealth temporarily removed from the owner's immediate control and possession is exempt from the annual Zakat levy. This narration highlights the Shia emphasis on possession (*qabd*) as a condition for Zakat liability, distinguishing between static wealth and capital in circulation. It serves as a practical legal mechanism for wealth preservation and circulation within the community, ensuring that temporary liquidity does not trigger immediate fiscal obligations.
